name: Concept E: high nodes, rockers on the front-hoop upper node and the rear top corner
summary: Every rocker pivot and coil-over chassis end is bracketed off a welded frame node. Front: the rocker sits behind the front hoop's upper node, on the outboard-rear side of the hoop leg, with its rod pickup above the hoop corner; the coil-over runs diagonally down behind the hoop leg to an eye beside the front-hoop side node (the UCA rear-pivot node), and the pushrod is mounted on the UCA, close to its outer ball joint. Rear: a transverse bell crank sits above the rear top corner (the UCA rear-pivot node), between the main-hoop brace and the engine-mount diagonal; its inboard arm drives a near-vertical coil-over, inboard of the PST rail, down to an eye beside the rear bottom corner (the LCA rear-pivot node). The rod comes from the LCA. The run shows zero evaluator fails on both axles and both corners, but the front only gets there at the edge of the limits: pivot 56.7 mm and coil-over end 59.7 mm from their nodes, which misses the 50 mm aim, and rocker and coil-over 5.2 mm from the tubes. The front also needs the pushrod on the UCA, so the UCA takes the spring load in bending, and it puts the coil-over's upper end inside the front-hoop opening. In return, the brackets load welded joints, not mid-span tubes. At the front-hoop nodes the rod and coil-over lines come out nearly parallel, which raises the rocker pivot reactions on both axles. The rear has thin but positive margins and keeps the coil-overs low. MR 0.80 at ride is the comparison query, not a choice.
pros: Zero evaluator fails on both axles and both corners against the chassis as updated and the engine on its mounts. The linkage was swept to the damper end stops (front -36.4 / +35.4 mm, rear -36.1 / +35.4 mm) and, at the front, over the full rack travel of +-38 mm.

Rear brackets at welded joints. The rocker pivot is 51.2 mm from the six-tube rear top corner node (-1461, 210, 328; 3DSketch7, PST, Tri_Tras), with its bracket foot 29.2 mm away on the Tri_Tras main-hoop brace, 42 mm from that tube's end at the node. The coil-over chassis eye is 54.4 mm from the five-tube rear bottom corner node (-1441, 175, 129; 3DSketch6, PST), with its bracket foot 45.3 mm away on the PST rail, 30 mm from its end.

Front brackets at welded joints. The rocker pivot is 56.7 mm from the four-tube front-hoop upper node (-89, 157, 561; FRONTO HO, Tri_Frente, Tri_Meio), with its bracket foot 33.4 mm away on the hoop leg, 40 mm from its upper end. The coil-over chassis eye is 59.7 mm from the five-tube front-hoop side node (worse corner: the right one, node (-106, -250, 319)), with its bracket foot 42.1 mm away on the rearward Tri_Meio tube, 42 mm from the node.

Rear kinematics: MR 0.7765 / 0.8000 / 0.8168 over +-25 mm (+5.0 %), equal 8.53 mm damper margins, rocker rotation -14.2 / +14.0 deg to the end stops, transmission angles at most 11.8 deg (rod) and 14.6 deg (coil-over). The rod is almost transverse (7.1 deg in plan, 53.3 deg from horizontal) and 362.5 mm long, at 1.60x the wheel load (1183 N at ride). It takes 12.8 kN of wheel load to buckle the 16x1 steel reference tube.

Rear clearances to the engine and drive train: chain and sprockets 12.8 mm (estimate), engine features 79.4 mm, drive shaft 10.6 mm (estimate). Coil-over body 10.8 mm and eyes 12.6 mm from the PST rail, left-to-right 112.4 mm.

Front kinematics: MR 0.7611 / 0.8000 / 0.8235 (+7.8 %), equal 8.56 mm damper margins, rocker rotation -20.9 / +20.1 deg, transmission angles at most 17.7 deg (rod) and 23.0 deg (coil-over). The UCA-mounted rod is short, at 335.6 mm and 1.59x the wheel load (930 N at ride). It takes 15.0 kN of wheel load to buckle the reference tube. Rod to wishbones and tie rod 18.9 mm, rim not reached by the rod, rack 179.9 mm, steering column 126.4 mm (estimate), left-to-right 240.8 mm.

The rear coil-overs sit low, with a moving-mass height of 273 mm (front 436 mm). The CG moves -1.42 mm against the project's seed layout and the tilt-table angle is 62.238 deg (reference 62.132 deg), with the estimated 1.3 kg coil-over + 0.3 kg rocker per corner.
cons: The front only just passes. The rocker is 5.19 mm from the Tri_Meio tube leaving the front-hoop upper node (at the droop stop) and the coil-over body is 5.18 mm from the Tri_Meio leaving the side node (at ride), against a 5 mm limit. The coil-over end is 59.7 mm from its node (limit 60) and the coil-over is 1.34 mm from the 'Ressalto-extrusão2' box (believed to be the leg template) at the droop stop. A millimetre of CAD change at the front hoop can turn any of these into a fail. The front pivot misses the 50 mm aim (56.7 mm).

The front pushrod is mounted on the UCA at (-5.24, 492.96, 386.17), not on the upright or the LCA. The UCA carries the rod force (930 N compression at ride, about 2.8 kN at 3x) near its ball joint, in bending, and so does its ball joint. In this search, the only zero-fail fronts with the rod on the upright put the rocker low at the side node and the coil-over up inside the front-hoop opening. Those fronts also needed a very large damper arm.

The front damper pickup sits at (-155.7, 156.6, 482.8), behind the hoop and inboard of the hoop leg. From there the coil-over crosses the cockpit side diagonally behind the hoop leg, down to the side node, at roughly the driver's knee height. That space and the driver's knee and hand clearance are not modelled, and an FSAE leg-protection shield for moving suspension parts would have to fit there. The front rocker pickups reach z = 588 mm, above the hoop corner (z range 345.5-588.1 mm including the coil-over end).

At these nodes the rod and coil-over lines are close to parallel: about 12 deg (front) and 16 deg (rear) apart, from the run's spec points. The rocker reacts nearly the sum of both forces. Pivot reaction at ride is 1652 N front and 2087 N rear. Bracket couples at ride (upper bound, force x stand-off) are 55.2 / 30.8 N·m front (pivot / coil-over end) and 60.9 / 41.9 N·m rear, about three times that at 3x. A rocker plane this close to degenerate is also sensitive: small input changes turn the rocker axis.

The rear rocker is large. Its arms are 91.4 mm (rod) and 117.1 mm (coil-over), and the pickups span y = 82 to 267 mm, from the inboard damper pickup to the outboard rod pickup. It sits behind the engine, near where a differential and its mounts would go (not modelled). The rear rod passes 5.61 mm from its own UCA rear leg at the droop stop, and the rocker is 5.65 mm from the Tri_Tras main-hoop brace at the droop stop.

The rear coil-over runs inboard of the PST rail toward the rear axle line. It is 10.6 mm from the estimated drive shaft (limit 10) and 15.4 mm from the toe link at the droop stop. The drive-shaft and CV envelope is an estimate, so this margin is not secured.
Steering moves the front damper by 4.38 mm over the full rack travel, about the steering jacking of any mount.

Springs (220 lb/in, no preload) unseat at -23.7 mm front, inside the +-25 mm travel, and -30.0 mm rear, as with any layout at MR 0.80. No anti-roll-bar provision was designed. The roll budget asks about 56.7 N·m/deg front and 77.7 N·m/deg rear for the 1.0 deg/g query target (springs alone 1.21 deg/g).
not_checked: The engine's scanned mesh. MOTOR_FIXADO is placed by its four mounts but modelled only by its features and the plenum outline. The chain and sprockets (14/46 520 assumed) and the drive shafts are estimates. Differential, exhaust, intake runners, radiator and fuel tank are not modelled, and the large rear rocker reaches toward that region.

The UCA with the pushrod clevis on it: tube bending, the ball joint load and the clevis are not sized. The upright, hub and brakes are not checked, and only the 13-inch rim is checked against the rods.

Real part envelopes. All gaps use estimated diameters: rod 16, coil-over 60, eyes 40, rocker +-10 mm plates and +-20 mm pickup bolts, frame 25.4. Rocker plates, bosses, yokes and rod ends are not modelled. With 5.2 mm front gaps, any real part that is larger than its estimate decides the front layout.

Node brackets. The pivots sit 51-57 mm and the coil-over ends 54-60 mm from the node centres. The plates or gussets that carry them back into each joint between the tubes meeting there were not designed. Their stiffness, which changes the effective MR, is not modelled.
Structure: no load cases, stress, fatigue or sizing of brackets, rails, rockers, rods, wishbones or uprights. The 3x figures are hand estimates.
Travel limits: the damper stroke (57 mm) is an estimate and there are no bump rubbers, so the linkage runs to the damper's end stops.

FSAE rules and the driver: leg protection for the front coil-over and rocker behind the front hoop, and driver knee and hand clearance at the hoop. What the 'Ressalto-extrusão1' and 'Ressalto-extrusão2' solids are is not confirmed; only their bounding boxes are checked.
The MR 0.80 target, the 1.0 deg/g roll gradient, the 50 % front roll share and the 220 lb/in springs are design-intent query arguments, not derived targets.
